title: Farms: follow soil patches, not rectangles
applies_when: Selecting crop fields and exact growing-zone cells.
approach: Prefer nearby rich soil for fertility-sensitive crops when it is safe and accessible. Nearby ordinary soil can beat distant rich soil after travel and exposure are considered.

Choose crops using current native minimum fertility and fertility sensitivity. Potatoes tolerate poor soil relatively well; rice benefits more from rich soil. Low sensitivity does not remove the minimum-fertility requirement.
Player preference: trace suitable soil patches with exact irregular cell lists; exclude unsuitable holes rather than enclosing them in a rectangle. This preference is not a universal game rule.
Check season, temperature and available planting labor. Fast rice harvests cost frequent labor; long-growing crops need enough time and reserves to survive until harvest.
verify: Every selected cell meets the chosen crop requirements; the zone is actually sown and reachable.
reconsider: No safe eligible patch exists, the season is too short, or travel defeats the fertility benefit.
